description: Renovate runs from .github/workflows/renovate.yml, not the hosted app. That cron decides how often it runs; the schedule here decides what it may do. The whole of Monday rather than a window within it, because a scheduled workflow can start hours late and a narrow window is one it misses.
Nothing Renovate bumps here is something a consumer of the modules fetches, so no rule below uses fix or feat: release.config.cjs cuts a release from those, and a CI tool bump is not one.
rebaseWhen keeps branches current because protection on main is strict: without it every pull request goes stale as soon as anything else lands.

Automerge is on only where CI exercises the change: the action pins and zizmor run in every pull request's own checks. Task does not, see its rule below; the npm packages run only in release.yml, the setup-node version likewise, and the demo's Dockerfile is never built in CI, so those wait for a person. rebase is the only merge method the repository allows.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Off, because the token is not granted `Dependabot alerts: read` and without it Renovate only warns once per run and carries on. Granting it and turning this on is one change.

customManagers.description: Tool versions no built-in manager sees: TASK_VERSION in ci.yml, and zizmor, which ci.yml and the pre-commit hook in lefthook.yml both run and must run at the same version. The `renovate:` comment directly above each pin carries the datasource and depName, so the patterns know no special cases; both zizmor pins share a depName and therefore move in one pull request. scripts/check-renovate.sh asserts these patterns still match every annotated pin and that every pin is annotated, because the failure mode is silent: Renovate opens no pull request, for ever.

packageRules.description: Everything in a workflow or action file: a `uses:` reference, or a step input such as setup-node's `node-version:`. No input is pinned today — Node is pinned in .github/ci/.node-version, which the ci scripts rule covers.

The `uses:` references — depType `action`, because a version input has no digest to pin — are pinned to commit shas with a version comment; Renovate maintains both. A release waits three days before it merges itself: the same actions run in release.yml holding a write token, which no pull request check exercises, and a compromised tag is usually caught and pulled within that time. The wait is the renovate/stability-days status Renovate posts on the branch, which is why the token needs `Commit statuses: write`: without it the post fails and Renovate abandons the whole run.

Task, zizmor and the tools the contracts run against: they change what the checks are, never what a consumer fetches. zizmor merges itself: Workflow audit runs the new version on the pull request. So do trivy, hadolint, gitleaks, checkov, kind and kubectl: Tool contracts runs the gates at the new version on the pull request.

Not Task, though. Its bump touches only ci.yml, and a workflow-only diff skips Consumer smoke — so the pull request would merge having run the modules under the new Task in Lint alone, never the way a consumer includes them.

semantic-release and its plugins, in the root package.json, move together; a preset ahead of the analyzer it plugs into is the usual way a release run breaks. They run only in release.yml after a merge, so nothing on the pull request proves them.
The CI scripts' dependencies and the Node they run on. Not release tooling: Lint type-checks and tests them and Consumer smoke runs them on the pull request itself.

The demo is a consumer of the library, not part of it. Its build image and its go directive are one toolchain: an image older than the directive cannot build the module, so the two move in one pull request.
